newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Rafsanjani presents budget to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Rafsanjani presents budget to parliament.

text.p: Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Sunday presented to parliament a budget 35 percent higher than the current year's with about 44 percent higher defence spending and less reliance on oil income.
Rafsanjani announced the 188 trillion rial ($108 billion at the official exchange rate of 1,750 rial to $1) budget -- Iran's highest ever -- for the Iranian year starting on March 21.
Oil exports remain the biggest source of state income and 63 percent of the total budget goes toward state industries and banks, down from 65 percent in the current year.

But the share of oil exports in government revenues -- at 41 percent following a downward trend -- has reached one of its lowest levels since the Islamic revolution which toppled the late shah in 1979.
Government revenue, excluding state industries and banks, is set at 74.9 trillion rials ($42.8 billion), 34 percent higher than last year's.

Some 41 percent or 30.7 trillion rials ($17.5 billion) is due to come from oil exports, 25 percent or 18.7 trillion rials ($10.7 billion) from taxes and 34 percent or 25.5 trillion rials ($14.6 billion) from other sources of revenue.
In the current year's budget oil income was forecast at $15.5 billion.
Rafsanjani said in order to "make sure that oil revenue materialises", the forecast was based on a lower price than the current rate. He did not gave any figures.
But Iran's head of the budget and planning organisation, Hamid Mirzadeh, was quoted by newspapers as giving the figure of $17.5 per barrel.
Rafsanjani said Iran's crude oil production capacity in August was "more than 3.9 million barrels per day".
